speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and fatigue; to help me narrow down the cause, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any associated changes in weight, appetite, or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your recent hiking, camping, and travel history alongside these symptoms, have you noticed any mosquito bites, insect stings, or exposure to ticks? Also, do you have any specific symptoms like fever, muscle pain, or joint swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

Your history of worsening fatigue throughout the day combined with new onset mild diplopia (double vision) strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction disorder. To confirm this, do you have any difficulty with swallowing, speaking slurred words, or lifting your eyelids? I will also need to request specific antibody tests.
